conviction_note: The quarter itself probably clears consensus: peers show home-furnishings share gains in the same window, and management called Q2 the tariff-margin trough. Against that, the stock is up 13.4% since the last print while the S&P fell, it sits about 4% under its 52-week high, the whisper ($2.23) is above consensus ($2.17), the skew is +19.5 points toward puts, and diesel hit a record during the quarter after a guide that assumed oil at about $90. The findings net to -0.4 and p_up of 48 on a 6.0% absolute move gives -0.24. The two measurements agree in sign and size, and both are essentially a non-result.

Revenue about $1.98-2.00B (+5.2% y/y on $1.88B), so the implied comp is about 4-5%. Whisper $2.23. No company quarterly guide. Street FY revenue $8.15B, below the bottom of the guided $8.17-8.37B. Two estimate sources agree within $0.02, so sizes are not capped.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY26 revenue about $8.15B (https://finviz.com/news/422854/..., 2026-11-15); FY EPS not found
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY26 revenue +4.7% to +7.2% (about $8.17-8.37B), comp +4.0% to +6.5%, non-GAAP operating margin 17.8-18.2%, tax rate about 26%, interest income about $25M; assumes current tariffs stay and oil stays elevated, and excludes refunds (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000719955/000071995526000203/exhibit991fy2026q2earnings.htm)
next_guide.basis: Peer demand (Wayfair US +11.4%, Arhaus written +13.9%) and the company's call of Q2 as the tariff trough support the revenue range. Record diesel during the quarter (Arhaus says fuel surcharges persist into H1 2027) and the 16-year-low housing turnover argue against raising margins. Most likely outcome: the revenue range is kept or nudged up and the margin range is kept.

findings.finding: Home-furnishings competitors that reported after WSM's Aug 26 guide show share gains for scaled players in a flat category. Wayfair Q3 (Jul-Sep) US revenue +11.4%, total +9.7%, orders +12.2%, with management calling the US category roughly flat. Arhaus Q3 comparable written sales +13.9% (Q2 +12.5%), new clients +20% in September, orders above $25k +35%. Home Depot Q3 comp +2.2%, 'exceeded our expectations'. The negative peer data point is RH: its Q3 revenue guide of +5-6% (given Sep 10) was below consensus. The street's ~5% WSM revenue growth (implied comp ~4-5%, a step down from 6.2% in Q2) looks beatable.
findings.link: Same US home-furnishings category and the same upper-middle-income customer. Wayfair is a direct online competitor; Arhaus and RH overlap with Pottery Barn and West Elm in furniture. Their quarters end one month before WSM's (Sep vs Oct). No shared customers or suppliers are disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comp beats have been bought only in 2026. Q2 FY26: comp +6.2%, revenue beat of about 2.6%, stock +1.15%. Q1 FY26 (May 2026): +6.49%. Every 2025 comp beat was sold (-2.9% to -4.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $1.98B (+5.2%) and the Nov 15 preview's 'implies cooling from 6.2%' show the street did not carry peer strength into WSM's number. Street FY revenue of $8.15B sits below WSM's own guide floor. If the peer reads were priced, estimates would sit at or above the guide midpoint. Partly priced, though: the stock is +13.4% since August.
findings.independence: Arhaus 8-K Q3 2026 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001875444/000187544426000036/q32026-earningsrelease.htm (2026-11-05); Home Depot Q3 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000354950/000035495026000184/hd_exhibit991x11012026.htm (2026-11-17). Three separate documents. The counter-reads are RH's Q3 guide below consensus (https://pulse2.com/rh-q2-revenue-rises-2-6-to-922-2-million-as-company-targets-up-to-7-fiscal-2026-growth/) and NRF furniture spending -2.6% in October (filed separately, in the housing finding).

findings.finding: Diesel set a record during WSM's Q3 (Aug 3 to about Nov 1): the US national average passed the prior record on Sep 3 ($5.82), topped $6 on Sep 10, hit a record $6.519 on Sep 22 and stayed above $6 until Nov 14. Brent was about $88-90 when WSM guided on Aug 26 and averaged about $124 in October. WSM's guide assumed 'oil stays elevated' at the August level. Arhaus (Nov 5) said fuel surcharges pressured Q3 margins and will persist into H1 2027. This argues for more freight and delivery cost in WSM's Q3 gross margin, and a reason not to raise the operating-margin range, beyond what the August guide carried.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross-margin and tariff-cost misses drove the 2025 sell-offs on beats: Nov 2025 -3.39% and Aug 2025 -2.91%, both on margin and tariff concerns. Q2 FY26 gross margin was down 160bp non-GAAP, and the stock still rose 1.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $2.17 (+10.7% y/y) still assumes margin expansion off a Q2 that management called the trough, and the preview names fuel only as a 'new pressure that could offset tariff relief', without a size. If priced, estimates would have been cut through October and the stock would not be up 13% since August. Partly offset: Brent is now at its lowest since August (about $96), which helps the Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Arhaus fuel-surcharge commentary, a different company and document: https://finviz.com/news/417330/arhaus-misses-on-profit-but-raises-its-revenue-outlook-as-demand-accelerates-faster-than-earnings (2026-11-05). Brent level at the guide: https://www.marex.com/news/2026/09/us-energy-market-commentary-august. This is macro-to-company transmission; WSM has not quantified its fuel exposure.

findings.finding: Housing turnover hit a 16-year low inside the quarter. October existing-home sales were 3.75m SAAR (-5.5% m/m, -8.8% y/y, the lowest since Aug 2010; consensus 3.85m), released Nov 12. The NRF/CNBC Retail Monitor had furniture and home furnishings at -2.62% in October and -2.7% in September. These are headwinds to the Q4 guide's tone and to the street's willingness to pay for a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WSM has repeatedly delivered comps 'despite the housing market' (Q2 FY26 CEO quote). Housing weakness was cited in the 2025 sell-offs but has not stopped the 2026 rallies.
findings.why_not_priced: Released a week before the print and widely reported, so it is mostly public. What is unpriced is whether management's Q4 guide reflects it; the street's FY revenue below the guide floor suggests analysts are already partly discounting it.
findings.independence: NRF Retail Monitor furniture -2.62% in October: https://www.retail-insight-network.com/newsletters/us-retail-sales-rise-for-13th-month-as-october-growth-slows. Counter: Wayfair says its category was flat while it grew 11%, which points to share gain over category decline (peer finding).

findings.finding: Expectations are high into the print. WSM is +13.4% since the Aug 26 report against S&P 500 -1.4% (to Nov 15), spot $259.4 is 3.95% below the 52-week high and 53.8% above the 52-week low, the Earnings Whisper of $2.23 is 3% above the $2.17 consensus, and the 25-delta skew is +19.5 vol points toward puts. The real bar is above consensus, and the last time this name ran into a print on a beat-and-raise path (Q2) a 2.4% EPS beat bought only +1.15%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: beat consensus, missed the whisper by $0.02, raised the guide, +1.15%. Q1 FY26 (after a spring sell-off): +6.49%. All four 2025 beats into a richer setup sold off 2.9-4.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew says the options market already pays for downside, so this is partly priced. What is not in the consensus EPS is the whisper premium and the run-up. A plain $2.17-2.20 print 'beats' consensus but misses the buy-side bar.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (sealed): run_up_20d +2.4%, pct_from_52w_high -3.95%, skew +19.54. The 13.4% figure is from the same preview document as the bar.

findings.finding: The street does not believe WSM's raised FY guide. FY revenue consensus of about $8.15B sits below the bottom of the company's $8.17-8.37B range (guide +4.7% to +7.2%, raised Aug 26 from +2.7% to +6.7%). WSM has beaten EPS consensus 7 quarters running (average +7.2%) and raised in Q2. Keeping or nudging up the revenue range would land above the street, a positive guide surprise in revenue terms. The margin range is the risk, given fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 revenue guide raise: +1.15% on the day, then +13% in the following weeks. Q1 FY26 reiterated guide: +6.49%. Aug 2025 raise: -2.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the guide, FY consensus would sit inside the range. A $20M+ gap between the street and the guide floor means a mere reaffirmation lifts street revenue. Partly offset because the whisper and run-up already lean toward a beat.
findings.independence: Company guide from the 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000719955/000071995526000203/exhibit991fy2026q2earnings.htm (2026-08-26). Beat streak (7 of 7, +7.2% average) from an aggregator in the search results, not independently verified.

findings.finding: Management called Q2 FY26 the peak tariff hit on merchandise margin (Q2 merchandise margin -230bp vs -100bp in Q1), so Q3 should show a narrower drag. No new furniture tariff took effect during Q3: the Section 232 increases on upholstered furniture and cabinets were delayed to 2027-01-01, and the Section 301 layer replaced Section 122 at roughly the same rate on 2026-07-24. Arhaus cut its annual tariff cost estimate from $50-60M to $30-40M on Nov 5. This sits inside the company's guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: a 160bp non-GAAP gross-margin decline was looked through (+1.15%). In 2025, tariff-margin worries drove -2.9% to -3.4% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management said it on the call and the guide carries it. What is unpriced is the size of the narrowing, which the fuel finding pulls the other way.
findings.independence: Section 232 delay: https://www.strtrade.com/trade-news-resources/str-trade-report/january/tariff-increase-delayed-on-furniture-kitchen-cabinets-vanities. Section 122 to 301 switch: https://borderbuddy.com/trade-tariff-news/section-122-is-out-section-301-is-in. Arhaus tariff estimate: https://finviz.com/news/417330/...

findings.finding: $29.3M of IEEPA tariff refund income was deferred into inventory at Q2 and is to be recognized as a COGS reduction in Q3 FY26, plus a $3.2M receivable. This will inflate GAAP gross margin and EPS (about $0.19/share pre-tax on about 118m shares) and is expected to be excluded from non-GAAP, as the Q2 refund was. The guide excludes refunds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26: a $167.8M refund made GAAP EPS $2.84 vs non-GAAP $2.10, and the stock rose only 1.15%. The market traded the non-GAAP line.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in August, so priced. It only matters if headline-GAAP algorithms misread it at the open or management uses it to firm Q4. No path to the guide is stated.
findings.independence: Same document as the guide; HomePage News restates it: https://www.homepagenews.com/retail-articles/williams-sonoma-cites-tariff-refunds-ai-following-q2-comp-gains-across-its-portfolio/

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No evidence that WSM's insider sales have moved prints; the CEO sells on a regular cadence.
findings.why_not_priced: Public on EDGAR. Small, and the sellers and whether these are 10b5-1 plans were not verified.

findings.finding: Short interest is moderate and falling into the print: 5.04% of shares outstanding with 5.86 days to cover at 2026-10-30, down from 5.60% at 10-15. There is no crowded short to squeeze and no build-up of bearish positioning beyond the option skew.
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral. It is recorded so the judges see that the downside skew is option demand, not a crowded short.

outside_window.finding: Section 232 tariff increases on upholstered furniture (25% to 30%) and kitchen cabinets and vanities (25% to 50%) are scheduled for 2027-01-01. They may enter the FY27 framing but do not take effect in the window.
Section 122 refund litigation: the Federal Circuit stayed the CIT ruling on 2026-06-11, with no merits opinion as of 2026-09-08. A future refund to WSM would be a one-off with no date.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the skew and the run-up on the setup: expectations are high, puts are bid and fuel is a cost headwind. It cuts against them on fundamentals: peer share gains and a guide the street sits below. So p_up stays near 50 rather than leaning hard either way.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): the peer-demand finding went from +0.8 to +0.5 because 2025 beats were sold. The separate -0.3 reaction-history finding was merged away as a duplicate so the lesson applies once.

Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): the fuel finding went from -1.0 to -0.8 and housing from -0.5 to -0.4. Both are macro transmission that WSM has not quantified, partly inside a guide that assumed elevated oil.
Lesson 7 (skew): the expectations finding went from -1.0 to -0.8. It agrees with a +19.5 put skew, so part of it is already in the price.
Pessimism artefact (lessons file, earlier lessons): p_up went from 47 to 48.
Left standing: the next-guide +0.8, the tariff-trough +0.3, the one-off +0.1, the insider -0.1 and the positioning 0.0.
